meta.surfaceDefinition: Capabilities describe only the named CMS route. Publishing means changing CMS content visibility, not deploying a frontend or verifying a live page.

evidenceBasisDefinition.Documentation reviewed: Assessment based on current official documentation, product announcements and public source repositories.
evidenceBasisDefinition.Connected: The route was authenticated and its advertised tools or commands were inspected.
evidenceBasisDefinition.Executed: At least one representative workflow was run against a controlled account or dataset.
evidenceBasisDefinition.Used repeatedly: The route was used across recurring production work, within the stated boundary.

setupDefinition.Easy: Connect a hosted service and approve access. No developer project or custom code.
setupDefinition.Moderate: Requires account configuration, credentials or a small amount of technical setup.
setupDefinition.Hard: Requires developer access, cloud or OAuth configuration, custom integration work or vendor approval.
setupDefinition.Specialist: Requires data engineering, infrastructure or statistical expertise beyond ordinary campaign operations.

actionDefinition.Yes: The evaluated route directly supports the action for its core objects.
actionDefinition.Partial: The action exists, but important objects, fields or workflows are missing or inconsistent.
actionDefinition.No: The evaluated route does not support the action.
actionDefinition.Depends: The action is determined by connected tools, permissions or custom configuration.
actionDefinition.N/A: The action is not meaningful for this type of tool.
actionDefinition.Unverified: The vendor has not documented a dependable boundary.

coverageDefinition.End to end: Completes nearly all of the recurring human job through the evaluated route.
coverageDefinition.Most steps: Completes most of the recurring job with a bounded human handoff.
coverageDefinition.Some steps: Handles useful parts of the job but leaves material work elsewhere.
coverageDefinition.Assist only: Supplies context or one narrow output rather than completing the job.
coverageDefinition.Depends: Coverage depends on the tools, data or permissions configured by the operator.
coverageDefinition.Specialist: Completes a specialist modelling or engineering job rather than ordinary campaign operations.

meta.commercialDefinition: Affiliate means a public commission-paying programme. Referral and Partner are shown separately and must not be described as affiliate programmes.

capabilityDefinition.Yes: The evaluated route directly supports the action for its core objects.
capabilityDefinition.Partial: The action exists, but important objects, fields or workflows are missing or inconsistent.
capabilityDefinition.No: The evaluated route does not support the action.
capabilityDefinition.Depends: The action is determined by connected tools, permissions or custom configuration.
capabilityDefinition.N/A: The action is not meaningful for this type of tool.
capabilityDefinition.Unverified: The vendor has not documented a dependable boundary.

wordpress-com.object: CMS content and its publication state

setup.note: Enable account MCP, connect with OAuth and select tool access; availability varies by plan, host and user permissions.

coverage.note: Documented post and page operations support drafts, updates and publication. Inspect the live tool catalogue for the connected site.

wordpress-com.blocker: Review changes before sending them: edits to a published post can go live immediately. Account tool settings are shared across connected assistants.
dailyTasks: Create a draft post and edit supported page content.
Publish approved posts through the tools enabled for the site.

wordpress-adapter.object: CMS content and its publication state

setup.note: A developer must install the adapter and supply the WordPress Abilities you need. Each Ability needs code, an input definition and a permission check.

coverage.note: The adapter connects agents to explicitly exposed Abilities; it is not a bundled, complete editorial toolset.

wordpress-adapter.blocker: Installing the adapter does not add editorial tools by itself. A developer must supply and check each task, including its permissions.
dailyTasks: Ask an assistant to run the Abilities registered on your site.
Expose a specific editorial task once its code and permissions exist.

webflow.object: CMS content and its publication state

setup.note: Authorise the right workspace and site role. Some design operations also need the Designer and its bridge app open.

coverage.note: Manage CMS collections and items, with partial localisation and additional design tools. Scope publication tools to the connected site.

webflow.blocker: New items in secondary languages still need another route. Some actions also require the right site role or an open Designer session.
dailyTasks: Update CMS items and supported page content.
Edit existing secondary-language items where the tool supports them.

contentful.object: CMS content and its publication state

setup.note: An administrator enables the required tools for each space and environment. You then connect the assistant with your own Contentful account.

coverage.note: Create and update entries, publish or unpublish content, manage locales and validate or schedule releases.

contentful.blocker: Check the user role and the tools enabled for the environment. Publishing in Contentful does not deploy your website; a local token-based connection has different access rules.
dailyTasks: Draft and edit entries, assets and locale content.
Publish approved content or organise it into a release.

sanity.object: CMS content and its publication state

setup.note: Connect with your Sanity account or a scoped API token. Select the correct project and dataset, and check the role’s write permissions.

coverage.note: Query with GROQ, create or edit structured content and publish drafts. Release versions require their own document IDs.

sanity.blocker: Check the schema, language setup and draft or release version before editing. Some document types skip drafts. Context MCP is a separate, read-only connection.
dailyTasks: Find and edit structured content with its schema in view.
Publish drafts or prepare content in a release version.

directus.object: CMS content and its publication state

setup.note: Use Directus 11.12 or later, enable MCP and create a dedicated user with suitable permissions and an access token.

coverage.note: Create and edit content using the configured collections, roles and workflows. Publication is a project-specific status or workflow, not a universal publish button.

directus.blocker: Your project defines which fields control publication and languages. Check the role’s edit and delete permissions before changing content.
dailyTasks: Find and edit content in configured collections.
Use the publication and language fields your project defines.

shopify.object: CMS content and its publication state

setup.note: A developer must create an authenticated app, grant content permissions and build the assistant’s API connection.

coverage.note: Create articles and pages with publication settings. This review does not establish a turnkey editorial MCP or general store-management coverage.

shopify.blocker: Review the copy and check the storefront after publication. Translation and editorial approvals need their own workflow.
dailyTasks: Create a blog article or information page.
Set its publication status or schedule when creating it.

woocommerce.surface: Official Abilities and MCP Adapter, developer preview

setup.note: A site administrator installs the MCP Adapter and creates a limited WordPress application password. Check the installed WooCommerce version and its Abilities before connecting.

dailyTasks: Find products for a content review.
Create or update the product fields exposed by the store’s Abilities.

coverage.note: Product query, creation, updates and deletion are documented. Editorial fields depend on the exposed Ability schemas.

woocommerce.blocker: The connection is a developer preview. Version 11.3 changes older connections; check support for extension fields and languages separately.

bigcommerce.surface: Pages V3 and Blog Content APIs

setup.note: A developer must create a store API account, grant content permissions and build the connection to the assistant.

dailyTasks: Update information pages and their metadata.
Create, edit and publish blog posts.

coverage.note: Read, create, edit and delete pages or blog posts. Blog posts have a publication flag; page visibility is not a complete editorial approval workflow.

bigcommerce.blocker: Review changes before writing, then check the storefront. Your integration must handle each channel’s content and language conventions.

adobe-commerce.surface: CMS REST API, PaaS or on-premises

setup.note: A developer must configure an integration with CMS permissions and connect it to the assistant. The team must confirm the store’s version, deployment type and content conventions.

dailyTasks: Update CMS page copy and reusable content blocks.
Prepare page changes and set the page’s active state.

coverage.note: Read, create, update and delete CMS pages and blocks. Page content and activation are separate fields; storefront delivery still needs a check.

adobe-commerce.blocker: Check the rendered page and use the editor for visual Page Builder work. This assessment does not establish a complete approval process or Adobe Commerce SaaS feature parity.
